title: Orion Live
tagline: The world's first real-time visual intelligence agent built to truly remember and understand the world as it unfolds
description:
Orion Live is the app behind Orion, a hybrid edge-server architecture designed to be an intelligent, interactive, and deployable visual perception agent that can truly 'remember' and 'understand', the world as it unfolds with a focus on being open-source, real-time, and privacy-first. While there are tools like OpenAI Sora and Gemini Live, the problem with them is that they are often slow, require steady cloud processing, and are solely focused on short, user-based interactions. For example, imagine you are a blind person who really needs assistance from a tool like this, and imagine that every aspect of your life and every moment and interaction is sent to some Google server hundreds of miles away and you have no clue with who's accessing that data and what they're doing with it. With Orion, I aim to change that by providing a system architecture that can run on an entirely local architecture, split processing on edge devices, and provide real-time responses to user queries while maintaining a high quality of output, privacy, and security in various types of environments, maintaining 24/7 context and memory of the world as it unfolds.

This is both a research project and consumer facing product I'm still actively working on developing and prototyping. You can find the initial prototype demo at the Orion github monorepo (riddhimanrana/orion) or see my research at orionlive.ai/research

title: Dicy
tagline: A modern grade experience for Infinite Campus and Schoology across iOS, Android, and web
description: I reverse engineered Infinite Campus and Schoology to create a substantially better way for students to view grades, test what-if scenarios, calculate final-grade targets, and use a growing set of academic tools. Dicy grew to more than 1,500 users across four-plus states while facing direct competition from other student products. I rejected acquisition interest, kept innovating, and used product design and direct marketing to regain market share.

title: Let's Assist
tagline: Volunteer infrastructure for students, schools, and community organizations
description: Let's Assist replaces fragmented SignUpGenius forms, spreadsheets, emails, and paper hour logs with one platform for opportunity discovery, registration, coordination, and service verification. It serves more than 300 users and is actively used by Troop 941. I am working with SRVUSD IT and California IT in Education on legal and compliance approval while partnering with DVHS CSF and DVHS Speech & Debate for broader adoption.

title: Chomp
tagline: Diabetes tracking application built for Los Altos Hacks 24
description:
Chomp is a diabetes tracking application me and my friend Abinav Venkit developed for Los Altos Hacks 2024. The primary goal of this project was to create a tool that helps people with diabetes manage their condition more effectively. Initially, I had tried to identify the nutritional information of the food by web scraping images of popular foods, taking my own data, and creating our own in-house model which we would connect to a nutritional API. However, with our 24 hour time constraint, we quickly realized that wasn't possilbe and were only able to implement the OCR recognition feature, which allows users to take a picture of their food and get the nutritional information.

The app is built using Next.js, TypeScript, and Shadcn UI and uses the Tesseract.js library for OCR recognition. While we didn't create a full implementation of this app, it was a good experience learning to use machine learning libraries in a web application.

title: PyEcoHome Energy Tracker
tagline: Home energy tracking application built in Python
description:
PyEcoHome is a Python-based tool for tracking and analyzing home energy consumption. It helps users monitor usage patterns, identify savings opportunities, and make eco-friendly choices.
I built this for the 2022 Congressional App Challenge and got selected as a finalist. Both of my demo and submission videos are available on my YouTube channel.
